thread:
Alex: proposing a small, reproducible apples-to-apples playbook for kernel + batching + KV cache ablations. want to capture warm vs cold, tokenizer alignment, and identical decode params.
Maria: yes please — our last run had noisy p95 because of warmup mismatch. :eyes:
Sam: quick note: we need the same prompt set, same stop-seqs, and exact tokenizer alignment. differences there blew up token counts in our head-to-head.
Alex: agreed. my suggested test matrix: 3 kernels (fast-attn, tiled-gemm, default), 2 quant levels (fp16, int4), 2 warm states (cold, warm), and replay harness vs synthetic repeater. keep batch sizes {1,4,16}.
Jen: can you paste the harness config?
Alex: here — minimal config we used in the last repro:
```yaml
harness:
  mode: replay
  trace_dir: /replay/traces/2026-03-prefixset
  decode_params:
    temperature: 0.0
    top_p: 0.95
    max_new_tokens: 64
    stop_sequences: ["\n\n", "###"]
kernels:
  - fast-attn
  - tiled-gemm
  - default
batch_sizes: [1,4,16]
warmup_prefix_cache: true
quant: [fp16, int4]
```
Sam: nice. two additions: 1) pin tokenizer model and include token count for prompt+completion in outputs, 2) ensure same RNG seed and disable sampling (temp=0) when comparing logits/decodes.
Kevin: saw a regression in the nightly: p95 latency for tiled-gemm jumped ~18% after commit 7a3cde2. likely kernel routing fallback warmed up different.
Maria: can we attach the profiler flame for that run? CI-bot: loadtest complete — artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/rt-bench/1767009999/artifacts.tar.gz
Alex: pulled the profile. short summary: tiled-gemm had a hidden fallback to smaller tile size under certain seq_len=512 tails; caused extra memory copies and KV cache evictions.
Jen: that explains KV miss rate spike in the logs. we saw cache miss ratio go from 2% -> 14% at around 30s into the run.
Sam: numbers from replay run (prompt set A, 1000 requests, seq distribution matched prod):
- fast-attn fp16 batch=4 warm: p50=45ms p95=110ms throughput=32k tokens/s
- tiled-gemm fp16 batch=4 warm: p50=52ms p95=130ms throughput=28k tokens/s
- tiled-gemm int4 batch=4 warm: p50=48ms p95=125ms throughput=30k tokens/s
- default fp16 batch=4 cold: p50=120ms p95=310ms throughput=12k tokens/s
Alex: note the cold default result — KV warmup dramatically matters. we should standardize on a warmup protocol: send 5 synthetic prefix requests per model instance before starting measurement.
Maria: agreed. also we found tokenizer misalignment: one model variant used a different EOS token mapping -> stop sequences not firing, resulting in longer generations and overcounted tokens.
Kevin: recommendation: bundle tokenizer hash in the harness metadata and fail run if mismatch.
Jen: on batching heuristics: observed that dynamic batching helped tail when small latency SLO but hurt throughput for steady-state high-concurrency. short heuristic: prefer static batching for sustained qps, dynamic for bursty traffic.
Alex: logging checklist for apples-to-apples runs: 1) harness config (as above), 2) tokenizer hash, 3) kernel selection policy, 4) quant flags, 5) warmup protocol, 6) per-instance KV hit/miss timeline, 7) p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/s.
Sam: one more ablation idea: disable prefix KV caching entirely to measure base kernel perf vs when cache is on. that isolates cache correctness/performance tradeoffs.
Maria: when we run this, let's tag runs with branch + commit + CI artifact link. I'll schedule the full matrix overnight.
CI-bot: scheduled job 1767010001 started (matrix runs). ETA ~6h.
Alex: perfect — after runs land, let's meet to decide if we need a kernel routing patch (likely for tiled-gemm fallback heuristics).
Kevin: I'll draft the patch to prevent tile-size fallback for seq_len > 256 without explicit mem check.
Jen: thanks all. small action list: Maria (run matrix), Kevin (kernel patch draft), Sam (tokenizer hash check in harness), Alex (write up playbook).
Alex: plan to share an RFC doc in #eng-runtime with results and recommended production routing defaults. :thumbsup:
